data.name: Abtal
data.gender_notes: Abtal is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic history, Abtal refers to the noble women who embraced Islam and supported Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the early Muslim community during the period of early Islam. They are considered a source of inspiration and strength. The name Abtal carries the meaning “Mothers of the believers” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Abtal usually hope their child will grow to embody mothers of the believers and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the importance of family and support in the spiritual journey of life.
data.etymology: Abtal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mothers of the believers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abtal total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: أبطال
in_arabic.meaning: أصحاب الشجاعة و القوة في المعارك و الحروب
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أبطال مشتق من الجذر أ-ب-ط-ل، ويعني أصحاب الشجاعة و القوة في المعارك و الحروب. وردت هذه الكلمة في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران الآية 123 {وَلَم يَكُن لَّهُ مُؤْمِنٌ إِلَّا مِن كُلِّ طَائِفَةٍ مِّنَ الأَقوامِ أَبطَالاً}

in_urdu.name: ابطل
in_urdu.meaning: شجاع اور قوت کے مالک لوگ، بہادر
in_urdu.long_meaning: ابطل کا مطلب ہے شجاع اور قوت کے مالک لوگ، بہادر۔ یہ نام عربی جڑ أ-ب-ط-ل سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کسی کام میں بہادری اور قوت کا مظاہرہ کرنا۔ اسلامی تقالید میں، ابطل ان شخصیات کی خصوصیت ہے جو اپنی بہادری اور قوت کے لئے جانی جاتے ہیں

in_hindi.name: अबतल
in_hindi.long_meaning: अबतल नाम का अर्थ है बहादुर लोग, शूरवीर, वीर। यह नाम अरबी मूल अ-ब-त-ल से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है किसी कार्य में बहादुरी और शक्ति का प्रदर्शन करना। इस्लामी परंपरा में, अबतल उन व्यक्तियों की विशेषता है जो अपनी बहादुरी और शक्ति के लिए जाने जाते हैं

in_pashto.long_meaning: ابټال د هغو کسانو نوم دی چې د زړورو او قويو کسانو په مانا کارول کېږي، هغه کسان چې په جګړو کې يې ښه کار کړی. دا نوم د عربي کلمې أ-ب-ط-ل څخه اخیستل شوی چې مطلب يې د چا لپاره په جګړه کې د ښه کار کولو څخه عبارت دی

in_english.name: Abtal
in_english.meaning: Brave and powerful individuals, heroes in battles
in_english.long_meaning: The name Abtal originates from the Arabic root أ-ب-ط-ل (a-b-ṭ-l), which signifies bravery and strength, particularly in battles and wars. This term is mentioned in the Quran, Surah Al Imran, Verse 123. In Islamic tradition, Abtal refers to individuals known for their courage and power, often used to describe heroes and brave warriors who demonstrate extraordinary valor

data.cultural_impact: The term 'Abtal' holds a significant cultural importance in Islamic history as it refers to the brave and selfless women who stood by Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) during the early days of Islam when the Muslims were facing numerous challenges and hardships. These women not only embraced Islam but also provided moral support, encouragement, and assistance to the Muslim community, earning them the title 'Abtal' or 'The Mothers of Believers'. Their unwavering dedication and sacrifices have been etched in Islamic history and continue to inspire Muslims around the world to this day.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the term 'Abtal' holds immense significance as it represents the essential role of women in the propagation of Islam and the nurturing of the Muslim community. These women served as models of faith, courage, and resilience, demonstrating that every individual, regardless of their gender or status, can contribute to the growth and success of the Muslim ummah (community). Their stories of steadfastness, sacrifice, and devotion serve as reminders of the importance of holding on to one's faith in times of hardship and opposition. Thus, the legacy of the 'Abtal' continues to inspire and guide Muslim women and men, calling upon them to embody the courage and resilience of these early Islamic women in their own lives.
